_comment: Thresholds the quality gates judge against. Every one is a judgement about a
particular business rather than a fact about data, which is why they live here
and not in the code — a consolidated multi-plant extract and a single-warehouse
one do not deserve the same join floor.
A gate BLOCKS when crossing the threshold would make the report wrong in a way
its reader could not see. Dirtiness that shows up as an obvious hole is a WARN
and does not stop anything. Raising a threshold to get past a failure is almost
always the wrong move: the run can be forced through once with allow_degraded,
which records the override, and that leaves the gate in place for next time.
_sku_agreement_floor: Share of a document's item numbers that must appear in some other document. Below it, every join it feeds returns empty and empty reads as zero.
_product_family_coverage_floor: Share of demand SKUs carrying a product family, below which the coverage figure is put in the headline of the warning. This does NOT block: an item selling without a classified master row is the ordinary state of anything new or transferred in, and a planner who cannot get a report until master data is perfect gets no reports. The missing materials are counted instead, and `product_family_source` on every row marks which families were guessed from the part number.
_semantic_failure_ceiling: Failure rate above which a semantic assertion is treated as the wrong column rather than dirty data. Keep it high: 8% negative lead times is a finding the report carries, 100% is a mapping error.
_forecast_coverage_floor: Share of SKUs with demand that must come out of the forecaster with a forecast. Without one a SKU is planned against zero demand and is never bought until it stocks out.
_position_coverage_floor: Share of forecast SKUs that must have a row in the inventory snapshot. An absent position is planned as zero, so each one reads as a shortage and is bought again.
_median_history_months: Periods of demand at the median SKU, below which the model competition cannot run and every SKU falls back to the pattern route. Warning only.
_extract_staleness_days: Age of the newest date in the data. The run anchors to it rather than to today, so past this the plan is made as of a date that has moved. Warning only.
